topic: GLM-5.3 went open-weight but its smallest build outsizes every consumer GPU
title: GLM-5.3 is free. Can your GPU run it?
description: GLM-5.3 just went open-weight, and the smallest GGUF build is 93.09 GB. That is more than any consumer GPU holds, including the 32 GB flagship card. The catch is the architecture: 18B active parameters ride on 320B total, and memory follows the total. You'll learn the one-line memory check that tells you whether a release fits your machine before you download a single gigabyte. Sizes are from the Unsloth GLM-5.3-Flash GGUF listing; Unsloth's own guide points 128 GB unified-memory machines at its 3-bit build. Subscribe to Build Local AI for what actually runs on the box you own. (Narration is AI-generated.)

narration_full: GLM five point three went free today. Your GPU still can't have it. Unsloth's smallest build is ninety-three point zero nine gigabytes of storage. Open weight promised you could run it. Eighteen billion active parameters, a size your card handles. The full model holds three hundred twenty billion parameters. Those are specialists behind a receptionist. She wakes a few per word, then re-picks. Anyone might be next, so everyone stays in memory. It serves machines holding one hundred twenty-eight gigabytes of unified memory. Processor and graphics share the pool. Usually the belief holds: shrunken builds fit your card. This one's the exception. The license opened. The memory didn't. Run the check: your machine's memory against the smallest file. If yours is smaller, close the tab.

notes_for_review: All numbers verbatim from the brief: 93.09 GB (UD-IQ1_S), 320B/18B, 128 GB devices; nothing rounded, the full 'point zero nine' is spoken once. The hook and title say GLM-5.3 while the measured files belong to the Flash variant, the release's small model (full GLM-5.3 is 753B); the description names GLM-5.3-Flash, flag if narration should too. The 1-bit detail (even the one-bit quant is 93 GB) and the UD-IQ3_XXS name stay out of narration to hold the number band at five; the description carries the 3-bit pick. The receptionist's limit (re-picks every word) sits in the same beat; the on-screen line 'Memory follows total, not active' is the script's single not-X-but-Y and it is on screen only. s7's etched GLM-5.3 die is the loop-anchor recall exception, digits recalled visually and spoken in s1.
